title: Anime OP Style Dance Animation
description: A detailed animation prompt for generating a fast-paced Japanese anime opening style dance, focusing on precise hand movements, cell-shaded aesthetics, and character consistency.
promptText:
Prioritize the analysis of character information from the reference image, extracting and maintaining features such as facial features, hairstyle, hair color, eyes, skin, clothing, accessories, body type, color scheme, and atmosphere. Rather than mere visual reproduction, extend the extracted colors, textures, and ambiance into text, lighting, hand trajectories, backgrounds, camera work, and impact frames.

A bright, fast-paced Japanese metaverse anime opening-style dance. The character faces forward and, synchronized with a light rhythm, performs a series of movements in quick succession: raising both hands to the sides of the face -> extending one hand diagonally upward -> placing the other hand on the hip -> small steps to the left and right -> quickly crossing both arms in front of the chest -> opening both hands wide outward -> leaning the body diagonally while slightly lifting one leg -> alternately pointing left and right with index fingers -> shaking both hands slightly beside the cheeks. Both feet remain on the ground.

The movements should not be too large but fine and fast, slightly comical and cute. Clearly show the poses of the arms, wrists, and fingertips. Focus on upper body and hand choreography rather than intense hip-shaking. Include momentary still poses followed by rapid transitions to different poses. The expression is energetic and happy. The camera should basically be a full-body shot from the front. Style: Japanese full-color anime, TV anime style, cell-shaded, flat coloring, smooth lines and fills, and brisk editing like an anime OP.

title: Anime Dance Video in Pop-up Book Style
description: A comprehensive Grok Imagine prompt for a 6-second anime dance video, focusing on character consistency, multi-camera coordination, and a colorful papercraft-inspired aesthetic.
promptText: # 6-Second Pop-Up Step Dance Video Prompt Use the character in the reference image as the sole protagonist. **6 seconds, 24 fps, vertical 9:16.** High-quality Japanese full-color animation. Art as refined as a theatrical anime movie, smooth body movements, rich facial expression changes, and naturally swaying hair and costumes. In a world of a colorful pop-up picture book, the protagonist performs a light step dance, creating an ultra-short dance video that is easy to play repeatedly on social media. ## Core Objectives * Hook viewers with both movement and expression in the first 0.3 seconds * Create a dance that utilizes footwork and a sense of rhythm different from previous works * Include a signature move that can be remembered after just one viewing * Use 5 cameras with detailed cut-ins to create pace and flow in the video * Create a loop structure that returns from the end to the beginning without feeling unnatural * Prioritize the protagonist's cuteness, friendliness, and energy * Structure the video to lead to saves, repeat plays, and imitation of the choreography ## Character Consistency The protagonist is the character from the reference image themselves. Maintain the following features seen in the reference image across all cameras, poses, expressions, and frames: * Hairstyle * Hair color * Shape of bangs * Eye color * Facial features * Skin color * Physique * Head-to-body ratio * Perceived age * Costume * Costume color scheme * Shoes * Accessories * Overall atmosphere Do not change faces or physiques even when cameras switch. Do not allow character changes, costume changes, hairstyle changes, or disappearance of accessories. Keep fingers in natural shapes and correctly depict left and right limbs. ## Setting The setting is a miniature dance stage created inside a giant pop-up picture book. Place the following decorations on a 3D floor that looks like an open page: * Clouds made of paper * Small star-shaped lights * Colorful building blocks * An arched background * Round stage lights * Small shapes like confetti The background colors should center on cream, coral pink, sky blue, lemon yellow, and lavender. Give the background a sense of three-dimensionality, but do not let it stand out more than the protagonist. Do not feature any persons other than the protagonist, dancers, audience members, or animals. ## Music **Completely original Japanese vocal track.** Do not make it resemble existing songs, anime songs, popular hits, or nursery rhymes. Bright and cute, up-tempo J-POP/anime-pop style. Do not include a short intro; start the vocals, beat, and melody simultaneously from 0 seconds. Use the following sounds in the music: * Light drums * Bright synthesizers * Small hand claps * Bell-like high notes * Bouncy bass * Cute accent sounds that feel like 'pon,' 'pah,' and 'kira.' Synchronize the choreography, camera switches, and background movement with the beat. The song should be approximately 5 seconds long, naturally ending the vocals and melody around 5.0 to 5.3 seconds. For the final 0.7 seconds, leave only a short lingering sound and sound effects that lead into the loop. Do not display text, subtitles, or lyrics. ## Video Concept The protagonist moves left and right on a small stage, performing a bright and cute dance combining bouncy steps and handclaps. Clearly show the following full-body movements, not just the upper body: * Steps opening toes left and right * Small lateral movements * Movements tucking knees inward * Rhythmical up-and-down movement of shoulders * Light turns * Handclaps synchronized with timing * Final one-legged balance pose Do not use intense acrobatics or large jumps. Make the choreography easy for anyone to imitate and want to dance along with the sound source. ## Signature Move Use the 'Pata-Pata Step' as the unique signature move for this video. 1. Open both hands outward at shoulder height. 2. Quickly flick wrists in and out twice. 3. Simultaneously open toes in the order of right, then left. 4. Cross both hands once in front of the chest. 5. Vigorously open the crossed hands diagonally upward. 6. Lift one leg slightly, tilt the head, and freeze with a smile. Perform hand and foot movements to the same rhythm, creating choreography that can be remembered just by its silhouette. Do not center the choreography around hearts, pointing, cheek-side peace signs, or blown kisses. ## Pop-Up Effects Unlike the previous work's crayon-style effects, use a 3D papercraft expression that looks like paper cutouts layered together. Motifs to use: * Small triangles * Colorful circles * Paper tape * Zigzag lines * Miniature clouds * Star-shaped paper pieces * Semicircular arches * Spring-like lines * Small confetti * Wavy ribbon-like paper Effects should appear as if popping out from the stage floor or background. Use the following movements: * Rising from the page * Folded paper opening * Bouncing once like a spring * Swaying slightly left and right * Scattering as confetti * Retracting back into the page Do not overlap too much on the protagonist's face or body. Use them to reinforce the direction of movement, foot landings, and the moment of handclaps. ## 5-Camera Configuration Use 5 cameras, but do not simply cycle through them every second. Insert short 0.2 to 0.5-second cut-ins in the middle of a longer main shot, changing perspectives according to the beat. ### Camera A: Front Wide Camera Main camera showing the protagonist's full body and the entire stage. An angle where choreography, footwork, and lateral movement are clear. Slightly dolly back and forth to follow the protagonist's movement naturally. ### Camera B: Low-Angle Camera from Diagonally Below Capture the protagonist from a low position in front of the stage, looking diagonally up. Emphasize foot landings, opening/closing of toes, and the swaying of the costume. Do not use an extreme low angle; maintain cuteness. ### Camera C: Right-Front Tracking Camera Run parallel to the protagonist's lateral movement from the front right. Show the coordination of face, shoulders, waist, and arms. The protagonist returns their gaze to the lens once during movement. ### Camera D: Top Camera from Directly Above Show floor shapes, foot trajectories, and paper effects in a circular composition. Use briefly as a beat accent rather than for long periods. ### Camera E: Face and Upper-Body Close-Up Camera Show changes in expression, handclaps, and head-tilting movements. Not a static close-up of the face; slide slightly sideways following the protagonist's movement. ## Camera Direction Do not use flashy glitches or flashes for camera switches. Use the following natural transitions: * Cut at the moment the protagonist's arm crosses the screen * Cut at the moment paper tape passes in front of the screen * Change the angle at the moment a foot lands on the floor * Connect directions according to the protagonist's turns * Use match cuts utilizing the background arches Even when cuts change, accurately connect the protagonist's arms, legs, body direction, and movement position. Ensure the same action doesn't rewind midway or suddenly become a different pose. ## 6-Second Timeline ### 0.0–0.7 seconds **Camera E: Close-up of face and upper body.** The protagonist is already in rhythm at the start. Bounce both shoulders alternately while quickly opening both hands beside the face. Change from slightly widened eyes (as if surprised) to a joyful smile. Around 0.2 seconds, background paper arches rise all at once. Small star-shaped paper pieces pop out from both sides of the face. The camera pulls back briefly once to transition to the next full-body shot. ### 0.7–1.6 seconds **Camera A: Front wide.** The protagonist moves two small steps to the right. Open both hands outward on the first step and clap in front of the chest on the second step. At the moment of the clap, a circular paper effect pops open from under the feet. Use knees and toes softly so the entire body appears to bounce. ### 1.6–2.0 seconds **Camera B: Short low-angle cut-in.** Capture the moment the protagonist lands their right foot on the floor and points their left toe outward. Triangles and zigzag lines pop out from the floor upon landing. Hair and costume hems sway with a slight delay. The protagonist's hand crosses in front of the screen at the end of the cut-in. ### 2.0–3.0 seconds **Camera C: Tracking from front right.** The protagonist performs the first half of the 'Pata-Pata Step' while returning to the left. Open both hands at shoulder height and flick wrists in and out twice. Simultaneously open toes in the order of right, then left. Look in the direction of travel at first, then send a gaze to the camera on the final wrist flick. Background paper tape waves according to the protagonist's movement. ### 3.0–3.4 seconds **Camera D: Short top-down cut-in.** The protagonist crosses both hands in front of the chest and brings both feet together in the center. Circles and stars drawn on the floor rotate once around the protagonist. Confetti spreads outward but disappears quickly to clean up the screen. ### 3.4–4.5 seconds **Camera A: Front wide.** The protagonist widely opens both crossed hands diagonally upward, completing the 'Pata-Pata Step.' Continuously bounce shoulders twice and take small steps in the order of right foot, then left foot. Background clouds and star-shaped lights move up and down alternately in sync with movements. The camera slowly approaches the protagonist. ### 4.5–5.1 seconds **Continuous cut from Camera B to Camera C using a turn.** Start a small half-turn movement from a low angle. Switch to the front-right tracking camera mid-turn to connect the movement seamlessly. After completing the turn, the protagonist lifts one leg slightly and opens both arms diagonally. Hair, costume, and paper tape stop with a soft delay in sync with the final note of the song. ### 5.1–6.0 seconds **Camera E: Dynamic close-up.** The protagonist lowers the lifted leg while returning both hands to shoulder height. Lightly tilt the head to the opposite side and smile joyfully. Not a wink closing one eye, but a bright laugh while looking at the camera with both eyes. Surrounding paper effects are stored away as if being folded back into the page. End by returning to the same starting posture with hands at shoulder height. End just before the shoulders enter the next beat; looping will connect naturally to the shoulder movement at the beginning. ## Facial Expression Acting Do not keep expressions static even within the short duration. * Beginning: Slightly surprised eyes * First half: Joyful smile * Gaze return to camera: Slightly mischievous expression * Signature move: Confident smile * End: Friendly and bright smile Avoid excessive funny faces or expressions where facial features deform greatly. ## Virality-Focused Direction * Both characters and background move simultaneously from the start * Include expression changes within 0.3 seconds * Give distinct characteristics to foot movements as well as hand movements * Insert short cut-ins synchronized with the beat * Place the core of the choreography around the 2-3 second mark * Match the final pose with the starting preparation posture * Create a silhouette that looks cute even when paused * Use compositions where face, hand, and foot movements are distinguishable even on small screens * Do not increase information too much; focus attention on the protagonist ## Constraints * Do not feature any persons other than the protagonist * Maintain the character from the reference image in all cuts * Do not change face, hairstyle, hair color, eyes, physique, head-to-body ratio, or perceived age * Do not change or lose costumes, shoes, or accessories * Do not allow character changes during camera switches * Clearly differentiate the use of the 5 cameras * Keep actions and positions continuous even when switching cameras * Do not cut off the feet too much from the screen * Do not include unnatural high-speed spins or large jumps * Do not distort the number of limbs or joints * Do not use excessive camera shake, motion blur, or fisheye distortion * Do not use live-action style explosions, smoke, fire, or lightning * Do not use glitches, screen splits, or strobe lighting * Do not display text, subtitles, lyrics, logos, UIs, or watermarks * Do not reproduce existing songs or existing choreography ## Output Ideal Establish a strong opening hook, light footwork, a memorable signature move, detailed perspective changes with 5 cameras, synchronization with music, and a natural loop within the short 6-second duration. Create a cute, up-tempo, viral-specialized animated dance video that makes viewers want to replay it and imitate the 'Pata-Pata Step' to the music.

title: Seamless Monsoon Rain Loop
description: A complex, multi-part prompt for a perfectly static camera shot of a rainy scene with flickering lamps and water ripples.
promptText:
Static locked-off tripod shot, camera completely still. NO zoom, NO pan, NO push in or out, NO camera movement of any kind. The frame stays EXACTLY the same size and position from first to last frame for a seamless loop.

Only these elements move, gently and continuously: heavy monsoon rain falling steadily and streaking through the warm lamp light, raindrops splashing softly and rippling the still reflecting pool, the brass oil lamp flames (diyas) flickering warmly, hanging lamps swaying almost imperceptibly, wisps of mist drifting slowly in the background, faint distant lights shimmering through the rain.

Keep all motion calm, slow, and natural so the beginning and end of the clip look nearly identical. Smooth cinematic seamless loop, no cut, no jump, no scene change, no camera drift.

title: Catholic Mouse Priest in Brooklyn
description: A cinematic video prompt for a photorealistic sequence featuring a mouse priest in a cassock navigating the bustling and oversized world of Brooklyn.
promptText:
15-second cinematic sequence, ultra-photorealistic, Pixar-level realism with live-action lighting, 4K, shallow depth of field, natural camera movement.

A tiny gray field mouse dressed as a humble Catholic priest wears a perfectly tailored black cassock with a white Roman collar sized for a mouse. He carries a tiny worn leather satchel filled with miniature prayer books and hurries with determination through the overwhelming streets of Brooklyn, New York.

The camera begins at mouse-eye level as enormous human shoes thunder past like moving buildings. Yellow taxis roar overhead. The vibration of subway trains can be felt through the pavement. Steam rises from street grates, creating towering clouds around him. Coffee cups, newspaper pages, and autumn leaves swirl through the air like giant objects in his world.

The little priest expertly dodges bicycle wheels, pigeons, rain puddles the size of lakes, and the shadows of hurried commuters, always remaining calm and joyful. Sunlight reflects warmly off the brownstones while church bells faintly ring in the distance.

The camera follows him as he reaches an old Brooklyn brownstone. At the base of the wide stone staircase leading to the front door is a tiny arched wooden church built into the foundation beneath the steps. It has stained-glass windows, a miniature brass bell, flower boxes, and a glowing lantern over the entrance.

The mouse priest smiles with quiet satisfaction, unlocks the tiny wooden door with an antique key, steps inside, and gently rings the little church bell as warm golden light spills out onto the sidewalk while the bustling human world continues completely unaware above him.

Highly cinematic, heartfelt, whimsical but grounded, realistic textures, authentic Brooklyn atmosphere, emotional storytelling, smooth tracking shots, no dialogue, natural ambient city sounds only.

title: Cowboy Playing Harmonica Technique
description: A detailed instruction for generating a video of a cowboy playing a harmonica, focusing on realistic breathing, hand movements, and technique.
promptText:
Once the cowboy begins to play, he’ll breathe from his stomach, not just his mouth. He’ll keep his lips relaxed and use his tongue to block the holes so he only plays one clean note at a time.
When he wants that deep, emotional, crying sound, he’ll cup his hands around the harmonica and open and close them while playing — that’s the hand wah.
He’ll be switching smoothly between blowing and drawing air, shaping each note with his tongue and throat so the harmonica actually sings.
That’s how it will look once the cowboy begins to play.
